components.gap: Reconstruct Eberhardt-Glymour's exact treatment (HHL vol.10 ch.10, pp.357-389) with every actual definition and claim. Missing: their display of the four axioms Univocality, Normalization (both clauses), Addition (with A.B implies not-C and existential r = p+q) and Multiplication (existential w = p.u) as printed pp.370-371 (the routed text explicitly declines to present this surface, reichenbach-probability-logic.tex 91-94); their composite formulas P(A v B) = P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B|A) and P(A = B) = 1-P(A)-P(B)+2P(A)P(B|A) (p.370); their claims that the axioms give only finite additivity in contrast with Kolmogorov, that the chain rule needs the fourth axiom, and that the axioms do not secure a sigma-field (van Fraassen 1979) (p.371); the rule of induction as a metalanguage rule not reducible to the object language, with Peirce's self-correcting method (pp.371-372); the coordination/isomorphism account with the inclined-plane example and the cloth-cube realism (pp.360-361); the three-part justification of the straight rule (higher-order probabilities, regress truncated by blind posits, finite convergence, 'simpler') (p.362); the formalist/Hilbert, positivist ('negativist'), von Mises and 1944 rejection-of-classical-logic influences (pp.357-359); blind posits as implicit flat priors, Reichenbach's claim that the straight rule equals a first Bayesian update under a flat prior and that appraised posits are informative priors, and the atom-decay single-case example (pp.373-374).

Preserve Eberhardt-Glymour's full historical argument and chronology. Missing: the 1915 thesis (causally independent identical trials, synthetic a priori causality, convergence in probability rejected as circular, transcendental principle of lawful distribution) and the authors' critique (pp.363-364); the 1927 notes and Hertz, the reversal of priority between causality and probability, elliptic single-event causation (p.364); von Mises' randomness conditions (after-effect, place selection) versus Reichenbach's normal sequences as a strict superset (pp.364-365); the gravitational-constant cross-induction with X = I(|M-gamma| <= delta), sequences a, b, c (moon, planet, Cavendish) and the second-order probability q (pp.365-366; routed lines 452-458 keep only the 0.8/0.7/0.79 arithmetic); the theory reference class filled with conservation-of-energy and entropy rows, the Maxwell/Bohr quotation, the Mercury footnote, and the singleton-class triviality critique of 'narrowest class with stable statistics' (pp.367-368); the rejection of many-valued modal logics (p.372). Section 5 in full: Popper's two routes and his two objections to the theory-class route, the regress-to-zero argument and Reichenbach's letter to Russell (a: 3/4, b: 1/2) (p.378), the Popper/Nagel 10%-disconfirmation-gives-0.9 objection, Reichenbach's 1949 p.436 schematization reply and the authors' critique (pp.378-379), Nagel's review points and the Hertz 1936 exchange, Creary's four conclusions (p.380), Nagel's account of scientific practice, the Tarski/Nagel extensional/intensional dispute and Reichenbach's 1939 reply (pp.380-381), Russell's prime-number ordering example and the Keynes contrast, Russell's certainty quotation and three-horned summary, his finite-sequence proposal, Nagel's translation dilemma and Reichenbach's formal/applied distinction with the non-Euclidean analogy (pp.381-382). Section 6 in full: the anti-Popper asymmetry argument, the fruit-vendor criticism of corroboration, the Carnap/principle-of-indifference criticism and its sigma-field irony, Hempel-Helmer-Oppenheim maximum likelihood and independence, Fisher likelihood versus inverse probability, the raven Bayes-rule treatment, and the grue argument with Reichenbach's narrowest-reference-class quotation and the authors' rebuttal (pp.382-384). The routed text gives these only as one-sentence mentions (lines 479-535).

Give Eberhardt-Glymour's worked cases, limitations and comparisons with philosophical, mathematical and empirical claim types kept apart. Missing: the commentary's four aims (a)-(d) and verdict that the logical machinery is unneeded (pp.384-385); the hierarchical-Bayesian hyper-parameter comparison as the authors state it (p.367); the clairvoyant argument as reported from the 1949 text p.476 with the authors' assessment (p.376; routed lines 418-425 source it to the 1937 French original instead); Reichenbach's acknowledgement of rival rules, his 'unbiased and functionally simplest' defence and the authors' rejection (p.376; routed theorem lines 396-412 states the rival rules but not this argument); the pragmatic justification and the claim that knowledge of the limit makes no difference to practice (p.376); the comparison with parametric (Gaussian) practice, non-parametric asymptotic normality and simulations as 'appraised posits' (pp.376-377); footnote 12 on straight rule versus Bayesian update; Reichenbach's k-dataset procedure p_f for functional forms and his resort to a simplicity-preferring Bayesian account, and the noise/metaphysical-uncertainty allocation argument (p.386). Present: the three uncertainty types (530-535), the noise-free fit (537-552), the straight-rule pointwise boundary (396-412).
